symbols.name: _build_parser
symbols.note: Builds and returns argparse.ArgumentParser for daedalus improve subcommand.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: Entry point for daedalus improve; parses args, builds queue, and optionally attempts one candidate.

claims.text: Rank the repo's own work by measurement and, with --once, attempt the top item in an isolated worktree. NEVER applies anything: the output is a patch plus a gate verdict for a human to promote or discard.
claims.why: The claim that it ranks work and produces a patch/gate verdict is not verifiable from this chunk alone; it depends on build_queue and review_packet which are not defined here.

claims.text: There is no --apply flag and there will not be one here.
claims.why: The argument parser does not define an --apply flag, and the epilog states it will never be added.

claims.text: Exit codes for --once: 0 = a gated candidate patch is waiting for you, 2 = the attempt ran and changed nothing, 3 = a source could not be consulted, so 'no candidate' is NOT evidence that there is no work, 1 = anything else (gate failed, runner failed, no candidate).
claims.why: The exit codes are defined by EXIT_BY_STATE, EXIT_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, EXIT_FAILED etc., which are not defined in this chunk. The actual mapping cannot be verified.

claims.text: Default behaviour with no flags is the DRY RUN. An operator who types daedalus improve to see what it does must not thereby start a model run in a worktree -- the destructive-by-default reading of an ambiguous command is the one that has to be wrong.
claims.why: In main, if args.once is False (default), it prints the queue and returns early without running any attempt, confirming dry-run behavior.
